customManagers.description: The pack CLI is downloaded by tag inside a RUN, where no manager looks. Match the ENV pin and track buildpacks/pack releases. Release tags carry a leading `v` that the download URL adds back itself, so store the bare version.

packageRules.description: Everything that pins the Go toolchain moves in one PR: the two .tool-versions pins (depNames `golang` and `golangci-lint`), the Dockerfile's `golang:<ver>-alpine` builder stage, and the `go` directive in builder/go.mod. The workflows no longer appear here because they read the version out of .tool-versions via setup-go's go-version-file. golangci-lint especially cannot lag: it type-checks through a vendored x/tools that only reads export data from Go releases it already knows about. minimumReleaseAge is off for the group because it is what splits it: the Docker datasource reports no releaseTimestamp, so a base image can never age, while .tool-versions can. Whichever side is ready first ships alone, because Renovate drops pending upgrades from a branch that has any ready one. CI gates the group instead of a soak.

A pin fixes a floating tag to the version already in use, so there is no newer release to age. Renovate synthesizes pin updates with no releaseTimestamp, and the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour of timestamp-required holds those pending forever.

The Docker datasource reports no releaseTimestamp for these tags, so timestamp-required leaves every base image update pending forever. That is invisible when a dep is alone on a branch -- it just never ships -- but in a group it is worse: Renovate drops the pending upgrade and ships the rest, which is how `golang:1.25-alpine` got left behind while .tool-versions moved to 1.27.2 in #53. Age these on the version the registry reports instead of refusing to age them at all. Applies to the `docker:<ver>-dind` final stage too. Why the timestamp is missing: Renovate reads `tag_last_pushed` from hub.docker.com 100 tags at a time, but Docker Hub answers anonymous requests past offset 1000 with `403 pagination offset too large for anonymous requests; sign in to page further`. library/golang has ~5100 tags and library/docker ~3100, so the walk always dies on page 11, Renovate falls back to the registry v2 tag list, and that carries no timestamps for any tag -- discarding the 1000 it had already collected. That is deterministic for any official image, so it will not age out on its own; only Docker Hub credentials would fix it. This rule is what puts `WARN: Some release(s) did not have a releaseTimestamp ... proceeding` on the Dependency Dashboard. The warning is expected and names no dep, so read it here: it comes from `docker:<ver>-dind` alone. `golang` never reaches the check, because the `go runtime` rule above sets minimumReleaseAge to null and the behaviour is only consulted once an age applies -- do not read this rule as what holds that group together, and do not narrow it to `docker` on the strength of that, which would re-arm the #53 trap for the next base image added here. Renovate can mute the warning with logLevelRemap; deliberately not used, because it is the only signal that something skipped the soak.

pack ships inside the image, so a bump to it is a user-visible change to the build environment rather than a library detail. Record it in the changelog with the bump itself; reconstructing it from git log at release time is how entries get missed. The command has to match allowedCommands in .github/workflows/renovate.yml, which is set from RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS and compared against the rendered string, not the template.

Renovate ignores indirect Go dependencies by default, so security advisories against them never turn into fixes. Enable them, but hold routine updates behind a dashboard checkbox so that every transitive bump doesn't become a PR; vulnerability fixes skip the checkbox on their own.

The AWS SDK is split across many separately versioned modules that release in lockstep. One PR each would outpace prConcurrentLimit, so group them. Keep this rule below the indirect one: a branch waits for approval if any single update in it does, and this group holds both direct and indirect modules.
